column1: # GE-T10's false-friend list for the subject-parts pass (CHANGELOG 1.12.0, the `Lindenbaum`
# cost): single words scored by `smysl_text::scope::derived_candidates` over the committed
# corpus (`../gold/corpus.smy`), each with the entity it names or `-` for none. The pass runs
# only when nothing else in a question names an entity, so a word is scored alone.
# WHY THIS LIST. Rules 22 and 23 found 32 of 32 subjects in `questions.tsv` and left one cost
# recorded: a German word that merely begins like a name (`Lindenbaum`, James Lind). Russian has
# the same cost through a suffix: `холерический` is "choleric", a temperament, and its stem less
# `ическ` is `холер`. The rules below are scored here, on words written after the rules were
# declared and before any code, whose result was taken first (`false-friends-baseline.txt`). No
# rule is added or changed after a run of this list.
#   24. German: a name of fewer than five letters is a compound's first part only when a hyphen
#       or the adjective ending `sch` follows it (`Lind-Versuch`, `Lindsche`), never a bare
#       letter (`Lind|enbaum`, `Snow|board`). A name of five letters or more is unchanged.
#   25. Russian: `ическ` is no longer a relational suffix; `атическ` stays (`миазм|атическ`).
#       A disease's adjective is `-н-` (`холерный`), and `-ическ-` on its root names something
# The guard rows (an entity expected) are the words rules 22 and 23 must still find.
# EXPECTED, WRITTEN BEFORE ANY RUN. Rule 24 does nothing for a long name, so `Jennerwein` (a
